findings.detail: v1.18.0 requires Kubernetes 1.29–1.33; the cluster runs 1.28, which is also already outside the source release's range (v1.17.0): the exclusion is pre-existing — this upgrade does not cause it, but the upgrade is still blocked. Plan the cluster upgrade at or above 1.29 before upgrading v1.18.0. The chart's kubeVersion constraint itself admits 1.28; the narrower supported range is the project's tested-matrix statement (Helm will not refuse the install).

### ACME HTTP01 challenge paths now use `PathType` `Exact` in Ingress routes

> ⚠️ Breaking change

We have changed the `PathType` for ACME HTTP01 Ingress-based challenges to `Exact`.
This security feature ensures that the challenge path (which is an exact path)
is not misinterpreted as a regular expression or some other Ingress-specific
(`ImplementationSpecific`) parsing.
This allows HTTP01 challenges to be solved when using standards compliant
Ingress controllers such as Cilium.

This change is incompatible with certain versions and configurations of the `ingress-nginx` Ingress controlle…

### ACME Certificate Profiles

cert-manager now supports the selection of ACME certificate profiles, allowing
users to request different categories of certificates from their ACME
Certificate Authority.
This enhancement leverages the latest [ACME protocol extension for certificate profiles (IETF draft)][rfc] and is supported by Let's Encrypt and other providers.
For example, Let's Encrypt offers the [`tlsserver`][tlsserver] profile for
standard server certificates and the [`shortlived`][shortlived] profile for
short-lived six-day certificates.
These new options provide users with greater flexi…

### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` is now `Always`

> ⚠️ Breaking change

We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` from `Never` to `Always`.

Why? Because the old default was unintuitive and insecure.
For example, if a private key is exposed, users may (reasonably) assume that
re-issuing a certificate (e.g. using `cmctl renew`) will generate a new private
key, but it won't unless the user has explicitly set `rotationPolicy: Always` on the Certificate resource.

This change is feature gated and is enabled by default…

### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` is now `1`

> ⚠️ Potentially breaking change

The default value for the `Certificate` resource's `revisionHistoryLimit` field is now set to 1.
This ensures that old `CertificateRequest` revisions are automatically garbage collected, improving resource management and reducing clutter in clusters.
Previously, if not specified, no limit was applied, potentially leading to an accumulation of stale `CertificateRequest` resources.
With this update, users no longer need to manually configure the revision history limit to benefit fro…

### Copy annotations from Ingress or Gateway to the Certificate

We've added a new configuration option to the cert-manager controller: `--extra-certificate-annotations`, which allows you to specify annotation keys to be copied from an Ingress or Gateway resource to the resulting Certificate object.
Read [Annotated Ingress resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/ingress.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate ), and
[Annotated Gateway resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/gateway.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate), to learn more.

1. We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` from `Never` to `Always`.

   > 📖 Read [Release 1.18 notes](../release-notes/release-notes-1.18.md) for more information..

1. We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` from `nil` to `1`.

   > 📖 Read [Release 1.18 notes](../release-notes/release-notes-1.18.md) for more information..

enrichments.title: ACME certificate profiles support added for CA flexibility
enrichments.content: This adds support for ACME certificate profiles per IETF draft, allowing selection of different certificate categories (e.g., Let's Encrypt tlsserver, shortlived). The environment uses cert-manager with Certificate resources. If ACME-based certificate issuance is configured, certificate profiles enable more granular control over certificate characteristics and provide access to provider-specific offerings.

enrichments.title: ACME test infrastructure upgrade has no operator impact
enrichments.content: This change upgrades Pebble (ACME test server) to v2.7.0 and modifies related E2E tests. This is test and development infrastructure used internally by cert-manager maintainers and has no effect on production cert-manager deployments or operator behavior.

enrichments.title: Breaking change to HTTP01 ACME challenge Ingress PathType
enrichments.content: This is a breaking change that modifies HTTP01 ACME challenge paths to use PathType `Exact` in Ingress routes. If cert-manager HTTP01 challenges are configured in this environment, this change improves security and standards compliance but may affect Ingress controllers that don't support `Exact` PathType. Review your ACME challenge configuration and Ingress controller compatibility to assess impact.

enrichments.title: Vault issuer config not used in this environment
enrichments.content: This change adds a server-name configuration option to the Vault issuer. The environment manifests show Certificate resources in use but no evidence of Vault issuers (ClusterIssuer or Issuer with vault provider). The values and manifest apiVersions do not indicate Vault issuer deployment. This feature does not apply to environments not using the Vault issuer.

enrichments.title: ACME profiles extension support applicability not determined
enrichments.content: This feature adds support for ACME profiles extension per IETF draft. The environment uses cert-manager but does not explicitly state whether ACME issuers (Let's Encrypt or other) are configured or what features are needed. If ACME profiles are used in your certificate issuance workflow, review the IETF draft to understand benefits.

enrichments.title: Let's Encrypt account key labeling impact unclear
enrichments.content: This change adds app.kubernetes.io/managed-by label to Let's Encrypt account keys. The environment runs cert-manager with Certificate resources but does not explicitly state whether Let's Encrypt issuers or ACME challenges are in use. If Let's Encrypt is used for certificate issuance, this label change improves resource tracking. Verify your Issuer/ClusterIssuer configurations to determine if Let's Encrypt is used.

enrichments.title: New certificate timing metrics enhance Prometheus monitoring
enrichments.content: This change adds certificate issuance and expiration timestamp metrics (certmanager_certificate_not_before_timestamp_seconds and certmanager_certificate_not_after_timestamp_seconds). The environment has prometheus.servicemonitor.enabled configured, indicating Prometheus monitoring is active. These new metrics can improve visibility into certificate lifecycle and enable better alerting and monitoring strategies.

enrichments.title: Ingress-shim annotation copying feature applicability unclear
enrichments.content: This change adds an ingress-shim option to copy extra annotations from Ingress resources to Certificate objects. The environment does not explicitly state whether cert-manager ingress-shim is deployed or used for Ingress-based certificate management. Verify if ingress-shim controller is enabled in your cert-manager configuration and whether you use Ingress resources with cert-manager annotations.

enrichments.title: ClusterIssuer now has convenient ciss short name alias
enrichments.content: This change adds the `ciss` short name as a convenience alias for the cert-manager ClusterIssuer resource. Operators using ClusterIssuer resources can use `kubectl get ciss` instead of `kubectl get clusterissuer`. This enhances usability in kubectl commands and scripts without breaking changes.

enrichments.title: Issuer now has convenient iss short name alias
enrichments.content: This change adds the `iss` short name as a convenience alias for the cert-manager Issuer resource. Operators using Issuer resources can use `kubectl get iss` instead of `kubectl get issuer`. This enhances usability in kubectl commands and scripts without breaking changes.

enrichments.title: HTTP-01 challenge RBAC disablement already configured
enrichments.content: This change adds support for the `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` helm value to disable HTTP-01 ACME challenges. The environment summary shows `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` is already set in the helm values. When upgrading to v1.18.0, this configured value will take effect, allowing cert-manager to drop pod-creation permissions if HTTP-01 challenges are not used.

enrichments.title: Certificate signature algorithm customization now available
enrichments.content: This feature allows customization of the signature algorithm used for certificate signing. The environment uses cert-manager with Certificate resources. If signature algorithm requirements exist (e.g., specific algorithms for compliance or compatibility), this feature enables flexible control over algorithm selection for generated certificates.

enrichments.title: DNS caching optimization applicability unclear

enrichments.content: This change switches cert-manager to use a local fork of the golang.org/x/crypto/acme package instead of the upstream version. This is an internal implementation detail that does not change operator-facing APIs, configuration, or behavior. No operator action or configuration changes are required.

enrichments.title: Ingress pathType changed to Exact for better security
enrichments.content: This change modifies Ingress resources created by cert-manager to use pathType `Exact` instead of `ImplementationSpecific`. The environment uses cert-manager with potential ingress-based certificate management. This improves security and reliability of ingress path matching. Review your Ingress configurations for any pathType dependencies.
